title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: In an agent, what decides which tool is called next?

options.text: The program's code, which runs the tools in an order the developer set
The model, which picks the next tool from the results so far
The user, who chooses each next tool from a menu at every step
The tool descriptions, which fix the order in which the tools run

items.stem: Every booking request needs the same steps in the same order: check the calendar, check training, then book. Which design fits best?

options.text: An agent, because a model should confirm each step is still needed
A fixed workflow, because the model must pick which tool comes first
An agent, because bookings change the calendar and need judgment
A fixed workflow, because the order is known before the request arrives

items.stem: In a fixed workflow, who decides the order of the steps, and when is it decided?
Student requests need anywhere from one tool call to eight, and nothing predicts which. Which design fits best?

options.text: An agent, because the model can choose how many steps each request needs
A fixed workflow, because every request must pass through the same steps
A fixed workflow, because it handles unusual requests more cheaply
A fixed workflow, because it can retry a failed step on its own

items.stem: Your budget is small, and one part of the assistant always follows the same path. Why is a fixed workflow usually the better choice there?

options.text: It keeps the model out of tool results, so answers are always correct
It uses a smaller model per step, so each call costs less
No model call is spent on choosing steps, so cost is predictable
It calls tools in parallel, so each request finishes sooner

items.stem: A Python script calls the model to read a manual page, then always runs check_calendar, then calls the model again. Is this a workflow or an agent, and why?
